items.q: What should you remember about **Unprepared = ramble by default**?
items.a: **without a fallback structure, you** speak messy thoughts aloud and lose clarity, authority, and confidence.

items.q: What should you remember about **Frameworks are the fallback**?
items.a: **when you have one,** you fall back on the framework instead of panic-scrambling.

items.q: What should you remember about **3-2-1 is a listicle, not a script**?
items.a: **three steps, two types/ways,** or one key idea; choose whichever fits fastest.

items.q: What should you remember about **Pick one mode only**?
items.a: **you do not deliver** all three variants; one is enough to sound structured.

items.q: What should you remember about **Pressure drill works**?
items.a: **random topic + 3-second countdown simulates real** Q&A; the student answered before the countdown finished because the framework made her feel ready.

items.q: What should you remember about **Body language follows structure**?
items.a: **prepared-with-framework speakers lean in** and move toward the audience; unprepared speakers shrink and avoid.

items.q: What should you remember about **Broader ecosystem**?
items.a: **Vinh positions this as one** of several communication frameworks (free 2-hour training covers 3-2-1 plus two others).
